Write KNBS data to a file, with its provenance

Source: R/write.R
knbs_write.Rd

Saves a table for colleagues who work in Excel, Stata, SPSS or anything that reads CSV, without losing where it came from. The format follows the file extension:

  • .xlsx - an Excel workbook with the data on a data sheet and an about sheet carrying the title, source, licence, release date, retrieval time and a ready-made citation.

  • .csv - UTF-8 CSV, with missing values as empty cells.

  • .dta - Stata, with the title as the dataset label.

  • .sav - SPSS, likewise.

  • .rds - R, keeping the object whole, metadata included.

CSV, Stata and SPSS files get a <file>.metadata.json provenance sidecar beside them, the same sidecar knbs_download_publication() writes.

Usage

knbs_write(
  x,
  path,
  format = NULL,
  metadata = NULL,
  overwrite = FALSE,
  quiet = knbs_option("quiet")
)

Arguments

x

A data frame: a result of this package, or any table.

path

Where to write. The extension chooses the format.

format

One of "xlsx", "csv", "dta", "sav" or "rds", to override the extension.

metadata

The provenance to record. Defaults to x's own.

overwrite

Whether to replace an existing file.

quiet

Whether to suppress the confirmation message.

Value

The path written, invisibly.

Details

Codes stay text: "01" is written as text in every format, never as the number 1. In CSV that means a quoted string, which Excel may still turn into a number when it opens the file; for Excel, write .xlsx.

List columns (the value labels of a survey's variables, for example) have no equivalent in these formats; each cell is written as JSON text, and the provenance says which columns were converted.

Stata limits variable names to 32 characters. Longer names are shortened

  • keeping a _code or _type ending, and staying unique - and the full name becomes the variable's label; the provenance lists every rename.

A table derived with summarise() or a pivot is plain data and carries no provenance of its own. Pass the source's with metadata = knbs_metadata(original); without it the file is still written, with a warning, and the about sheet or sidecar says no provenance was attached.

Excel output needs the writexl package and Stata or SPSS output the haven package; you are asked to install them if they are missing.

See also

knbs_metadata(), knbs_cite()

Examples

# The FinAccess file catalogue ships with the package, provenance and all
files <- knbs_finaccess_files(content = "data")
path <- file.path(tempdir(), "finaccess-files.csv")
knbs_write(files, path)                        # + finaccess-files.csv.metadata.json
#> ✔ Wrote /tmp/RtmpUVZNuQ/finaccess-files.csv (14 rows), provenance in finaccess-files.csv.metadata.json.
if (FALSE) { # interactive()
gdp <- knbs_abstract_table("2.2")
knbs_write(gdp, file.path(tempdir(), "gdp-by-activity.xlsx"))   # data + about sheet
knbs_write(gdp, file.path(tempdir(), "gdp-by-activity.dta"))

# A derived table keeps the source's provenance when you pass it on
totals <- dplyr::summarise(gdp, value = sum(value), .by = period)
knbs_write(totals, file.path(tempdir(), "totals.csv"), metadata = knbs_metadata(gdp))
}
